newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico, Central American nations vow to protect reef.
newsitem.headline: Mexico, Central American nations vow to protect reef.

text.p: Mexico, Guatemala, Belize and Honduras signed a landmark accord during World Environment Day on Thursday to protect the Caribbean's coral reef system, the world's second-largest.
Leaders from all four nations met at this world-famous Mayan archaeological site bordered by the Caribbean's clear blue waters and coral reef that sits just beneath the surface.

"Environmental protection is an effort that cannot be restricted to political boundaries between nations...We must all respect the environment of our neighbours," Belizean Prime Minister Manuel Esquivel said during the ceremony.
The 620-mile (1,000 km) reef is second in the world to the Great Barrier Reef, which spans 1,550 miles (2,500-km).
Eager to attract tourist dollars, the countries stressed that the coral reef was important for both ecological and economic reasons. They said the reef complemented the region's Mayan treasures.
"To kill it off would be collective suicide," Honduran President Carlos Roberto Reina said.
